independent.summary: `data: withEditableData(type, { ...BLOCK_DEFAULTS[type] })` shallow-copies `BLOCK_DEFAULTS.gallery`, so every gallery block created in one editor instance shares the *same* `images` array object (the spread copies the reference, and `withEditableData` leaves it alone because `Array.isArray` is already true). Add two gallery blocks to one entity, click "+ Add image" in the second and type a URL: the row appears in the first gallery too, and the save writes identical images into both blocks. The hydration path at line 260 has the same aliasing — `{ ...b.data }` keeps `props.initial.blocks[i].data.images`, so editing rows mutates the caller's object (the draft item in the draft-review screen) even if the user cancels. Both tests pass only because each exercises a single gallery block.

The human-edited-draft-item schema still validates blocks as `data: z.record(z.unknown())` and was not given the new `blockDataError` leaf, so a reviewer editing a generated item can store a gallery with a `javascript:` url; it is only refused later by `applyDraft`. The file documents itself as mirroring "what POST /entities would accept, rather than being a separate dialect", which is no longer true for gallery data (no entity is written, so this is a stored-draft defect, not a bypass into the graph).

The suite header says the MCP `create_entity` path "is covered by `tests/http/mcp.test.js`'s harness", but `tests/http/mcp.test.js` contains no gallery case at all — grep for "gallery" there returns nothing. Deleting both `blockDataError` calls added to `routes/mcp.js` breaks no test, so the file's own falsification claim ("no write path is a side door", "each group fails only for its own writer") does not hold for the fourth writer it names.

The save-time pruning only drops blank rows; a row whose URL is scheme-less (`images.example.test/x.jpg`) or otherwise unparseable is posted as-is and refused with a 400 whose message never reaches the user — `onEntitySaved` (WikiLayout.vue:1333) awaits `addEntity` with no catch, so the rejection is unhandled, the panel stays open and the save silently does nothing. There is no client-side URL check either (the `type="url"` input is not inside a `<form>`, so constraint validation never runs), which is the same "losing a whole save" failure the blank-row pruning was added to avoid.

triageGrades.reason: No auth, session, passkey or permission code is changed; the suite only registers users as fixtures.
No credentials, tokens or env secrets are added or read (the item deliberately avoids any storage credential).
No billing, pricing or paid-API path is touched; uploads/hosting (the cost-bearing half) are explicitly out of scope.
No deletions or migrations; the new validator is explicitly written so existing `{images: []}` / `{}` blocks stay saveable.
No outbound API client or service integration is added — the third-party image fetches are the browser loading `` URLs, not code calling an external API.
Only docs/roadmap/wishlist/decision-log prose changes; no version bump, CI, packaging or deploy configuration.

summary: The local review found nothing and its triage was right on every category, but it missed the aliased gallery `images` array in the editor plus three smaller validation/coverage gaps, so it contributed no signal beyond triage.
